thread:
sam (Support): Heads up — ACME reported their console shows a three-hour gap in hourly usage for 2026-02-18 10:00-13:00 UTC. They say tokens were used but the console shows zeros. :worried:

carlos (Customer Success): They said the app saw normal responses and billing events, just the analytics dashboard is empty. Asking for ETA; customer is worried about SLA.

sam (Support): I checked logs briefly — our billing events arrived, but hourly rollup job logged a warning around 10:07 UTC and then no writes for several partitions. Attaching small snippet: ```WARN rollup: missing manifest for partition tenant_id=acme-123 hour=2026-02-18T10:00Z```

dana (Data Platform): Hmm. I see the rollup worker fetches an S3 manifest for the hour window and then streams objects. If manifest reads 404, worker skips write for safety. Can you paste the full warn?

sam (Support): Full line: ```2026-02-18T10:07:12Z WARN rollup_worker::fetch_manifest error=NoSuchKey key=manifests/2026/02/18/10/tenant=acme-123.json```

dana (Data Platform): That key was removed. Looking at S3 audit, there was a lifecycle delete for prefix manifests/ applied accidentally during a migration the morning of 2026-02-18. It expired small manifests (24h rule) earlier than intended. Confirming now. :eyes:

mohit (SRE): If manifests are missing, downstream consumers skip aggregation. Any chance the objects themselves still exist and only the index manifest deleted?

dana (Data Platform): For a handful of hours the manifest was removed and some objects were present but unreferenced. I can run a reconcile: list objects under raw/tenant=acme-123/2026/02/18/10 and rebuild a manifest.

sam (Support): Customer wants a timeline and whether data can be backfilled.

olivia (Eng-Infra): We should avoid broad S3 list for many tenants. Plan: for affected tenants, reconstruct manifests from object keys then trigger rollup worker to re-ingest that hour. Dana, can you scope which tenants/hours are impacted?

dana (Data Platform): Initial query: impacted hours 2026-02-18 09:00-14:00 UTC across ~7 tenants; acme-123 is highest priority. I can emit a targeted backfill job that 1) rebuilds manifests, 2) pushes to the rollup input topic with original timestamps.

mohit (SRE): We'll need to coordinate retention window. Some objects are already in cold storage; if they were transitioned and deleted, we may need restore from Glacier. Any signs of transition?
dana (Data Platform): A subset (~2%) shows storage-class=GLACIER_IR. For acme-123 10:00 hour all objects are Standard, so immediate rebuild is fine. For others we'll need restore requests.

sam (Support): Suggested customer message: we found a misapplied S3 lifecycle rule during an infra migration that removed manifest files indexing hourly objects. We're rebuilding manifests and running a targeted backfill for affected hours. ETA initial fix for acme-123 in ~2 hours, full backfill for all tenants in 24-48h depending on restores. Approve? :thumbsup:

carlos (Customer Success): I'll send that with a note about mitigations and a follow-up once acme is reprocessed. Please DM me when acme re-ingest completes so I can update the customer.

dana (Data Platform): Running the manifest rebuild for acme-123 now. Command run: ```./tools/rebuild_manifest --tenant acme-123 --hour 2026-02-18T10:00Z --output s3://manifests/2026/02/18/10/tenant=acme-123.json```

deploy-bot: backfill-job-981 submitted by dana — status: queued

mohit (SRE): I'll watch the consumer lag and ensure we don't overload rollup workers. If we see spikes, we can throttle with the backfill-rate limiter.

olivia (Eng-Infra): Runbook note: add canary check for lifecycle rules targeting manifests/ prefix. Also add S3 object lock on manifests/ for 7 days during migrations. Filing infra ticket after this thread.

sam (Support): Update: dana reports the rebuilt manifest was published at 2026-02-18T11:05Z and backfill job started. Rollup worker wrote rows for acme-123 10:00 hour at 11:12Z. Carlos, please confirm customer sees numbers.

carlos (Customer Success): Pinged ACME — they confirmed the hourly line reappeared and looks correct. They're relieved. Sending official note.

dana (Data Platform): Next steps: 1) finish manifest rebuilds for remaining tenants (in progress), 2) queue restore tasks for Glacier objects (if any), 3) add automated alert when manifest key 404 rate > 0.5% for any hour.

sam (Support): Closing loop — no billing impact observed. Marking incident as "analytics-manifest-expiry" for postmortem. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
